critical_code_review_comments: utils/ai.py::_ai_chat retry-skip predicate uses substring match: `'not configured' in str(e)`. This is fragile — any future error message that happens to contain the substring 'not configured' anywhere would incorrectly skip the retry. Consider using a sentinel exception class (e.g. VertexNotConfiguredError) raised explicitly by _gemini_chat when config is missing, then `except VertexNotConfiguredError` for the skip branch. Also: the current substring check will match e.g. a Google-side error text like 'Model not configured for this project' — probably safe today but not intent-explicit.

utils/ai.py::_ai_chat retry does not distinguish retryable vs non-retryable transport errors. A Vertex 400 (bad request / safety block via `ValueError('Vertex AI response truncated/blocked ...')`) or 401 (auth) will still consume the 1.5s retry, then fall back to OpenAI — with identical result. Consider not retrying on ValueError variants that indicate a deterministic response-level failure (finish_reason != STOP, empty text, no candidates) since those aren't transport blips.
